thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU OOM spike detected on prefill workers in us-west-2. 6 containers restarted in the last 6m, node gpu-rt-12 involved. Paging @maria :rotating_light:

maria: I'm on it, grabbing context. Was there a deploy in the last hour?

sam: Not from infra, there was a model config tweak to prefetch/kv-cache yesterday (kv_prefetch=1.2) by ml-runtime. Could be related.

diana: Confirmed; we rolled a prefetch throttle change at 01:12UTC. Seen a rise in long-context requests (>= 100k tokens).

tess: Quick customer impact: CS reporting several 5xxs to Acme prod org, ~12% failure rate for embedding/chat requests. Lia is on the line with them.

lia-cs: Acme noticed streaming disconnects and retries around 20:40 PST. They're seeing higher latency as well. They're asking for ETA.

maria: OK mitigation plan - immediate short-term: disable kv_prefetch on prefill workers, throttle prefill window > 32k tokens, set routing to fallback model variant with smaller KV footprint. Can we do that now?

sam: I can patch runtime flags for the affected pool. Command I will run: 
```
curl -XPOST "$RUNTIME_API/pools/gpu-prefill/actions" -d '{"kv_prefetch":0, "prefill_max_window":32768}'
```
Will flip to conservative mode, expect ongoing requests to be rejected/redirected for the largest windows.

diana: Also recommend enabling early-trim for prefill streams: drop prefix tokens > 64k and return code 413 for unsupported length until we have a long-term fix.

tess: Lia, tell Acme we are applying mitigations now and will follow up with root cause and ETA. Use internal status page for next update.

lia-cs: Copy, passing along. They want to know if data was processed or dropped.

maria: No evidence of data exfiltration; requests either retried or failed at runtime OOM. We'll follow up with logs per request id.

sam: Ran quick nvidia-smi on node gpu-rt-12: 
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0   A100-80GB     On           | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off | 0                    |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:                                                                  |
|  PID   Type   Process name    GPU Memory |
| 12345  C      prefill-worker   66000MiB |  <-- two procs pinned near full mem
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
We see fragmentation: free mem scattered, allocation fails for large prefills.

diana: Also found CUDA error traces in recent container logs: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.1 GiB (GPU 0; 81.00 GiB total capacity; 78.9 GiB already allocated; 1.5 GiB free; 6.8 GiB reserved in allocator)
```
This suggests allocator reserved space but prefill spikes push over threshold.

maria: Good. Short-term actions executed: sam flipped kv_prefetch=0 and set prefill_max_window=32768 on pool. Tess, please confirm rollout.

tess: Confirmed rollout to pool gpu-prefill-12 -> new flag present on 6 nodes, traffic gradually shifting, circuit should start rejecting extreme windows.

lia-cs: Acme updated: they see fewer 5xxs after mitigations but still intermittent. They appreciate quick response.

sam: Will also drain node gpu-rt-12 and rotate workloads while we investigate fragmentation pattern. Triggering cordon + drain now: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-rt-12 && kubectl drain gpu-rt-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```

diana: I'll collect heap snapshots and NVML allocator stats for the containers on that node while it's being drained. Expect data in ~10m.

maria: Oncall handoff: I'm staying on for the next 45m and then will hand to sam if it's still active. @sam, take over if I need to step away.

sam: Roger. I'll monitor the drain and the autoscaler for additional capacity. If we see thrashing, we'll enable temporary rate-limiter per-org for large-context routes.

tess: Ops note: adding a short-term config to the router: max_prefill_tokens_per_org=20000 for free tier, 100k for enterprise with explicit approval. Rolling this in 2m.

diana: Preliminary root-cause hypothesis: allocator fragmentation plus aggressive kv_prefetch combined with a recent spike of extremely-long user prompts from a single org (not Acme) caused a chain of large allocations -> OOM -> container restart. Need a longer-term fix: allocator tuning, slab consolidation, and prefill trimming in the model server.

maria: Agreed. After stabilizing, plan: 1) repro locally with long-window synthetic prompts 2) test allocator change (reduce max_reserved_fraction) 3) add prefill circuit-breaker at router layer 4) consider coldmodel fallback for >64k windows.

lia-cs: Acme wants postmortem and ETA. Can we commit to a timeline for RCA and a mitigation release?

sam: Short-term RCA + mitigation doc in 24h, full postmortem within 72h. We'll provide per-request id logs to Acme by EOD.

tess: Noting runbook steps and updating incident channel. Adding quiet tag for customer comms.

diana: Uploading collected traces to s3://redwood-incidents/7932012345/trace.tar.gz once the drain finishes.

maria: Thanks team. I'll keep this thread updated. If any new restarts occur ping @maria directly. :thumbsup:
